pr.title: LF on every platform: content hashes survive a Windows clone (windows-portability.md chunk 1)
pr.head: 6d63b2b5b971c28f0a906985c59fb8054f9bf18f

summary: field is a command-line music production tool that keeps a project as a Git repository of text files and audio assets. Several of its answers come from file bytes as they sit on disk: the cache key of a SuperCollider render, the canonical-formatting check in field check, and the sha256 that pins each asset. Git for Windows defaults to core.autocrlf=true, which rewrites text files to CRLF line endings on checkout. A fresh Windows clone therefore produced different answers from every other platform, while git status stayed clean because Git compares normalized content.

This pull request is chunk 1 of the Windows portability plan. It adds a root .gitattributes that checks text out with LF endings everywhere and exempts audio and captured plugin state from any conversion. In the same diff, the plan moves from draft to in-progress and answers its open decisions, and docs/README.md names Windows and Linux as build-and-test targets rather than leaving them out of scope.

The pull request was opened in August against the older plan layout. Merges of main moved its plan edits onto the layout main adopted in #164, and a follow-up commit gave §6's last question its disposition, which fixed all four findings from the September review. This head merges main again after the keyboard-instrument stack (#178 to #182) and #159 landed. The pull request's own diff did not change.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• core.autocrlf: a Git setting. true, the Git for Windows default, converts LF to CRLF on checkout.
  • text=auto: lets Git decide which files are text and normalize their line endings.
  • eol=lf: checks text out with LF endings on every platform.
  • binary: Git's shorthand for -text -diff -merge, so no line-ending conversion.
  • Action key: the cache key of a build step, hashed from its inputs.
  • Asset pin: the sha256 recorded for a committed asset.
  • State blob: a captured plugin state file under shared/plugins/, named by its own sha256.

cards.title: Left for later
cards.html:
• Chunks 2 to 5: the MSVC build and paths, render determinism, the named-pipe transport, and a Windows CI job.
  • Projects made before #159: field init keeps an existing .gitattributes, so an older project needs * text=auto eol=lf added by hand, as docs/project-model.md says.

groups.title: One file makes the checkout byte-defined
groups.kicker: The root .gitattributes: LF for text, binary for audio and plugin state.
intro: Before this change the repository had no .gitattributes, so each clone's line endings followed the cloner's Git settings. On Windows that meant CRLF, and four things field computes from file bytes changed: the action key of an sc-render step, field check's canonical-formatting comparison, asset pins, and the check that a plugin state blob still hashes to its filename. The last one refuses to render rather than quietly differing.

The file sets two rules. * text=auto eol=lf tells Git to detect text files and always check them out with LF endings, whatever core.autocrlf says. The binary lines that follow exempt seven audio extensions and *.state from any conversion. For each attribute the last matching line wins, so the overrides must come after the * line.

No audio or .state file is committed today. The overrides exist so the first one arrives protected. Without them, Git's binary detection, which looks for a NUL byte, would treat a state blob that happens to contain none as text.

files.note: All of chunk 1: the LF rule, the binary overrides, and comments recording why each exists.

checks.text: git ls-files --eol at this head shows 325 blobs with LF endings and 6 with none. No blob carries CRLF and none is detected as binary, so this rule changes no committed content and no git add --renormalize step is missing.
The comment's claim holds: src/audio/plugins.ts:296-299 throws when a state blob's sha256 differs from its filename.

git check-attr gives text: auto and eol: lf for text, including creek-kit.scd and field's own sc/voice-render.scd and sc/voicer.scd, and text: unset for .wav, .aiff, and .state paths. With text unset, eol has no effect, so the binary overrides win. No nested .gitattributes exists.

groups.title: The Windows plan goes in-progress and answers its own questions
groups.kicker: The frontmatter flip, §2's decisions, the chunk 1 record, and §6's dispositions.
intro: docs/projects/windows-portability/readme.md is the plan for making field build, check, play, and live-render on Windows. Each plan in this repository carries status (draft, ready, in-progress, or completed) and priority (now, next, or later) in its frontmatter. Moving a plan to in-progress claims it is ready to execute, so the change that does it must answer, or explicitly defer, every question the plan still has open.
This diff moves the plan from draft at later to in-progress at now, and does that answering:

• §2 Decisions. The four open choices become decided: named pipes rather than loopback TCP for the daemon's control socket, no non-daemon playback fallback for field play on Windows, one socketPathFor function with a platform branch, and the docs/README.md scope change riding this diff.
  • §1.1 and §5. The prose now records that chunk 1 landed, with its Windows proof.
  • §6 Open questions. Each gets a disposition. Two are deferred to chunk 4 with their tests named. The 104-byte question is answered by §2.1 and §2.3. Whether anything else hashes on-disk bytes is answered by a grep of src/, whose conclusion still holds at this head.

checks.text: The readiness claim holds. Each §6 question carries an explicit disposition: the detached-spawn and WASAPI questions are deferred to chunk 4, the 104-byte question is answered by §2.1 and §2.3, and the hasher question is answered. §4's question about CPython and AF_UNIX sits in the out-of-scope list and needs no answer.

files.note: The plan itself: the frontmatter flip, §2 decided, §1.1 and §5 updated for chunk 1, and a disposition on each §6 question.

checks.text: project check reports the plans valid at this head, with status: in-progress and priority: now.
creek-kit.scd at this head is 2,252 bytes with sha256 49f970a7…, the LF form recorded a few lines below.

The disposition agrees with the plan: §2.1 decides named pipes, §2.3 says socketPathFor returns a pipe name on Windows, and §5's chunk 4 owns both ends of the transport. This fixes the last open review thread.

Non-blocking suggestion from the review: this list predates code main added since. src/generators/voice-render.ts (#182) hashes the instrument program and field's own sc/voice-render.scd and sc/voicer.scd into each MIDI take's render inputs, which puts it in the sc-render action-key family, with this repository's own checkout bytes reaching a project's cache keys. And land now also pins .notes.yaml MIDI takes, a text file, by sha256 in the ledger, not only .wav takes. Both are covered by the LF rule; the list should name them.

Every non-test hasher of file bytes still goes through src/hash.ts at this head. click.ts has no hash reference, remote/client.ts hashes network bytes, and graph/build.ts still defines actionKey, so the answer's conclusion holds.

groups.title: docs/README.md names Windows and Linux as build-and-test targets
groups.kicker: The V1 platform scope section, amended as the plan's §2.4 requires.
intro: The "V1 platform scope" section of docs/README.md says what version 1 of field supports and what it leaves out. It listed Windows and Linux as out of scope, although CI already builds and tests on Linux. This diff removes both from that list and adds a paragraph: they are build-and-test targets, not product platforms, and the product ships on macOS.
The plan made this change a precondition of its own flip to in-progress, which is why it rides the same diff.

files.note: Windows and Linux leave the out-of-scope list, and a new paragraph says what they are instead.

checks.text: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs pnpm build:native and pnpm test on ubuntu-latest, and linux-portability.md decision 5 calls Linux a build-and-test target, as this paragraph cites. Both links resolve, and no other root document states a platform scope that contradicts it.
